findings.title: OAuth 2 authorization code with PKCE is documented for user-authorized apps
findings.detail: GitLab supports authorization code flows, with PKCE recommended for client and server apps. Access tokens expire after two hours by default, so integrations must refresh tokens using the refresh_token attribute.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when customer users connect their own GitLab accounts through OAuth.

Authorization code (with or without PKCE) flow requires application to be
By default, access tokens expire after two hours (7200 seconds). Integrations that use access tokens must generate a new token with the refresh_token attribute. Refresh tokens can be used even

findings.title: read_api grants read access to the API for accessible groups and projects
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, and is sufficient for queries. It is broader than issue-only access, so the token can read other API resources the person can access; the app should use it only for issue-title reads.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the least-privilege read-only grant for listing issues in projects the connected person can access.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
Scope Access read_api Grants read access to the API. Sufficient for queries.
List all issues Lists all issues the authenticated user has access to. By default, returns only issues created by the current user.

findings.title: Connected person's project access determines returned issues
findings.detail: The API returns only data the authenticated person can access; unauthorized project fields may return null or 404 rather than an error. Checking that the connected person can access the target project is a user prerequisite, not an extra OAuth scope.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to each customer account whose project access is required for issue titles.

findings.title: Use keyset or offset pagination for issue lists
findings.detail: The project issues endpoint supports offset and keyset pagination; keyset is recommended for consecutive pages. Offset pagination is the default with per_page up to 100, and the app should follow only the supplied Link header for next pages.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when reading all matching issue titles across multiple pages.

evidence.quote: This endpoint supports both offset-based and keyset-based pagination. You should use keyset-based
Pagination GitLab supports the following pagination methods:
per_page Number of items to list per page (default: 20 , max: 100 ).

findings.title: Register the OAuth application before authorization
findings.detail: Authorization code flows require the application to be registered in the user's account settings. Registration provides the application ID and client secret, and a redirect URI must be configured, preferably HTTPS for production.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies before customer users can authorize the app.

steps.title: Register the GitLab OAuth application for the customer user
steps.detail: Developer registers an OAuth application in the GitLab user settings (Edit profile > Access > Applications) or, for group-owned use, in group Settings > Applications. Record the Application ID and Client Secret, and set the Redirect URI to the HTTPS callback of the integration. Use scope read_api only.
steps.doneWhen: Application ID, client secret and redirect URI are stored securely and the application lists read_api as its scope.

steps.title: Confirm the consent redirect and callback before code exchange
steps.detail: Send the customer user to the authorization URL with read_api scope, a state value and PKCE code_challenge. The user approves access in GitLab. Verify the callback returns code and the same state value. This is a consent step executed by the customer account, not the developer.
steps.doneWhen: The callback URL contains a code parameter and a state value matching the one generated before the redirect.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the returned code with the token endpoint using PKCE code_verifier. Public PKCE clients omit the client secret. Store access_token, refresh_token and expires_in. The access token expires after two hours by default.
steps.doneWhen: Token response contains access_token, token_type bearer and refresh_token.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles for an accessible project
steps.detail: Call the project issues endpoint with the access token in the Authorization header. Titles are at $[].title in the JSON array. Use the user-provided project ID (or URL-encoded full path) with provenance from the customer. A 404 or null means no access rather than an empty result.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returned with a JSON array where each element exposes a title string, and the Link header is inspected for next. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.title: Verify read-only boundary using a documented excluded read
steps.detail: Confirm the scope granted to the token using the token info endpoint, which reports the scopes attached to the access token. Verify the response lists read_api and no write scope. Inspect the outgoing request log for this integration to confirm no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE requests were sent to issue endpoints. Note that read_api is documented as read access to the API across all accessible groups and projects; the sources do not document read-only enforcement at the token level, so the scope check confirms the grant but does not prove writes are impossible. Do not send any prohibited write to test this.
steps.doneWhen: Token info response lists read_api scope without any write scope, and the outgoing request log shows only GET requests to issue read endpoints.
